---
title: "Data Infrastructure"
sidebarTitle: "Overview"
description: "The engines that get your data in and shape it: Airhouse, Airway, and Airform"
---

Data Infrastructure is the foundation of Oxygen, getting your data in and
shaping it into clean tables that your [World Model](/guide/build/world-model)
and agents can query. Three engines do the work:

- **Airway** *loads*: it extracts data from the systems a business already
  runs and loads it into the warehouse, moving only what changed.
- **Airhouse** *stores*: it is the managed, Postgres-compatible warehouse
  where that data lands, along with the facts
  [custom apps](/guide/build/custom-apps) record, with isolated databases and
  no long-lived keys.
- **Airform** *shapes*: it turns raw tables into clean, tested ones with
  version-controlled SQL models.

## One workspace, from source to model

A typical data stack is stitched together from separate products for moving,
storing, transforming, and defining data, each with its own configuration,
credentials, and release process. The seams between them are where numbers
drift and failures hide.

In Oxygen, every step lives in one workspace. Pipelines, models, and metric
definitions are files reviewed and deployed together through Git, alongside
the agents and automations that use them. A change to how data is loaded,
shaped, or measured is a single, reviewable change, and every number an agent
reports traces back to definitions you can read.
